question: In March 2025, Operation Brahma was launched to assist earthquake hit __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was launched in **March 2025** by the Government of India to assist Myanmar after a devastating earthquake caused widespread destruction and loss of life.
 
• This operation was part of India’s commitment to providing humanitarian aid to its neighbors under its **"Neighborhood First" policy**.
 
• The assistance primarily included **rescue operations, medical aid, and relief supplies**, as Myanmar faced severe challenges due to the earthquake's aftermath.
 
• The operation was conducted with the support of Indian armed forces, medical teams, and disaster response units to ensure the swift delivery of aid.
 
• India has a history of supporting its neighbors during crises, reflecting its role as a responsible regional power and its strong bilateral ties with Myanmar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India-Myanmar Relations:**

 
 
• Myanmar shares a **1,643 km-long border** with India, touching four Indian states: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram.
 
• India and Myanmar have close historical, cultural, and economic ties. Myanmar is a key partner in India’s **Act East Policy**.
 
• The two countries have collaborated on infrastructure projects such as the **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project** and the **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway**.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake in Myanmar (March 2025):**
 
 
• The earthquake caused significant damage to infrastructure, homes, and public services, displacing thousands of people.
 
• Many areas were left without basic necessities such as food, water, and medical care, prompting international humanitarian responses.
 
 
 
• **India’s Disaster Assistance Framework:**
 
 
• India has a robust disaster response mechanism led by organizations such as the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** and the armed forces.
 
• India has previously launched similar missions like **Operation Maitri** to assist Nepal after the 2015 earthquake and **Operation Dost** to aid Turkey and Syria in 2023.
 
 
 
• **Neighborhood First Policy:**
 
 
• India’s Neighborhood First policy focuses on prioritizing relations with neighboring countries to ensure regional cooperation, stability, and development.
 
• Humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR) operations are an integral part of this policy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Operation Maitri (Nepal, 2015):**

 
 
• Conducted in response to the devastating earthquake in Nepal, providing rescue and relief operations.
 
• Included the deployment of the Indian Air Force and NDRF teams for search and rescue operations.
 
 
 
• **Operation Dost (Turkey and Syria, 2023):**
 
 
• India provided aid after the massive earthquake in Turkey and Syria, showcasing its commitment to global humanitarian efforts.
 
• Assistance included rescue teams, medical personnel, and essential supplies.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Response in India:**
 
 
• India has a comprehensive disaster response system led by the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and specialized agencies like the **NDRF**.
 
• India is recognized globally for its quick and efficient response to natural disasters in the region.
